en.hubeali: Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the night in which to seek what is sought, when to bathe?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the beginning of the night; and if you so desire to, when you are standing (for Prayer) at its end’. And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the standing (for the Prayer), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be standing during its beginning and its end’.
en.sarwar: 3. Safwan ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the night during which one can appeal before Allah for one’s needs when it is the time for a shower. He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is at the beginning of the night, or if you like, at the end of the night as you wake up.’ I then asked about al-Qiyam (rising up) (for salat [prayer]). He said, ‘You may rise in the beginning or toward the end of the night.’”
